digest: blake2b-128 of the contiguous float32 feature row
finding: The corpus builder emitted 9 pairs of source chunks whose carved feature rows collide - 64 identical row pairs out of 1300000 rows, 0.00492 percent. The grouped split keeps each CHUNK ID wholly on one side, but it cannot know that two different chunk ids carry the same content, so 32 of those row pairs straddle the evaluation/pool boundary, spread over 6 of the 9 chunk pairs. Only ONE pair (44496 on the evaluation side, 48016 on the pool side, 26 of 26 rows identical) lands inside the blocks 0020 fits on, and it produces every collision the runner refused on: 8 rows of the 100000-row reproduction block and 2 of the 26346-row builder-matched block. NONE of the 9 pairs involves the extension corpus, and 0020's real-content fit corpus has zero rows byte-identical to any scored row, so the clause's own disjointness is intact. What the refusal caught is a property of the BUILDER's corpus, inherited unmeasured by every preregistration that has fitted on this pool and scored on this evaluation set since 0003 - including the 0.1965 reproduction rung 0020 uses as its control.
split: tools/pivot/run_carve.py grouped_split(y, g, 20260825, 0.2, 800000), 0003's, which the record has used since
why: Preregistration 0020's runner refused (exit 3) because its preregistered condition requires that no repro-block or matched-block row be byte-identical to a scored row, and 8 repro rows and 2 matched rows are. This artifact measures the cause across the whole builder cache, once, so the refusal can be read rather than guessed at.
